label: digit 3 input late in the original sequence (position >= 6)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively when the input token is the digit 3 during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at a late position. At positions 6-8 it fires on essentially every 3 (precision 1.0); at position 5 it fires weakly on a minority of 3s (the main source of missed activations, all in the lowest quartile). Never fires at positions 0-4, at <DEL>, or in the copy phase (even when 3 is input there), and essentially never on other tokens. Magnitude grows with position and with nearness to the end of the original sequence: top activations (~2.8) are 3 at position 8 as the last original token, and t=5 activations are around 0.3 of max.

issues: Minor factual error: the explanation says activations at t=5 are about 0.3 of the max. They are much smaller. In the test misses, t=5 activations on 3 sit at 0.01-0.06 of the max. The dev profile gives t=5 0.8% of the mass over 1947 active steps, which is roughly 0.04 of the max on average. This doesn't change the predicate, and it makes the t=5 tail even less important.

The t=5 tail can't be captured as a clean class. (phase==0)&(in_tok==3)&(t==5) has test precision 0.18 and recall 0.11. Adding L>=8 gives precision 0.18. So 3 at position 5 fires only rarely and weakly, and adding it would lower F1.

The other claims check out. There are 0 false positives on test (precision 1.0) and zero activation at t<=4, at <DEL>, and in the copy phase: (phase!=0)&(in_tok==3) predicts 90606 steps with precision 0. Non-3 tokens give only about 36 activations out of about 18.8k (v, d, 2, x, k), which is scattered noise. Mean magnitude per active step rises with t (from the dev mass shares: t=6 about 0.040e-3, t=7 0.072e-3, t=8 0.088e-3 per step) and with closeness to the end of the sequence (to_go=0 holds 57% of the mass).
The misses are almost entirely 3 at t=5. They hold 0.8% of the activation mass (mass recall 0.992), so there is no systematic gap.
